title: workflow-axa 2.8: a modular engineering workflow — delivery

snapshot.basis: Uncommitted working tree on 9daf507 at delivery, 2026-11-02. Validator PASS, 585 tests OK (11 host skips).

understanding: /workflow is now a small router to four phase skills (clarify, specify, execute, deliver). Matt Pocock's eight skills ship inside the package as separate skills. Every rule has one owner file. Two approval gates, with a combined message for small settled changes. Tested on Altinstar and Cheflabels worktrees and reviewed by Claude and Codex.
boundaries: No commits, pushes, installs or changes to the main Altinstar, Cheflabels or web repositories.
Strict UI kit reuse and historical report snapshots are unchanged.
Agent behavior was observed in one run per scenario, not measured as a rate.

sections.title: What was asked
sections.text: Refactor workflow-axa into a modular engineering workflow: better questions, a mutual agreement, specs and tickets, a central HTML report, test-first building, reviews, and an honest delivery report. Integrate Matt Pocock's grilling, implement-spec, code-review and tdd. Test on Altinstar-react and Cheflabels worktrees.

sections.title: What was agreed
sections.text: R1–R10 in PLAN, accepted through D5. During the work the user added: a Matt-style rewrite and a reader-first report (D6), vendoring the external skills (D7), separate skills and one owner per rule (D10), both gates in one message for small settled changes (D8), keeping the menu as it is (D9), and the HTML report for every plan approval unless declined (D11).

sections.title: What was built
sections.text: A 700-word router and four phase skills; eight vendored skills with adaptation sections; grilling owns all questioning; open_items.py, handoff messages, state lines and parallel tickets from the retro; a stricter delivery check in the report helper; the reader-first report layout.

sections.title: Decisions made
sections.text: D3 two approvals; D5 finish without another pause; D6 Matt style and reader-first report; D7/D10 vendored separate skills; D8 combined gates for small changes; D9 menu unchanged; D11 HTML report for every plan approval unless declined.

sections.title: Limits and open points
sections.text: Browser suites not run (no Playwright). Native discovery of the installed plugin in Claude Desktop and Codex not tested. Agents still sometimes skip nested steps (opening tdd first, record.py); each run is one sample. Changes are uncommitted; someone staged them at 15:12, later edits are unstaged.

sections.title: How it was checked
sections.text: Validator and 585 unit tests. About 30 live headless sessions on both repositories in six loops, each loading the exact candidate. Two retros: 55 past sessions and the evaluation sessions themselves. A retro over 55 past sessions. Independent reviews by Claude and Codex, four rounds in total.

sections.title: Delivery summary
sections.text: Delivered as partial: everything agreed is built and checked, with the limits listed above still open.
